subject: matrix could not be inverted, model not identified

messages.author: 0357983fe6002975
messages.subject: matrix could not be inverted, model not identified
parts:
When I specify my model as follows:

mod<- "
         mediator~ a * independent+ covariates
         dependent~ b * mediator+ cp * independent+covariates
         # corr errors
          mediator~~ dependent 

         # indirect and total effects
         ab := a * b
         total := cp + ab"

set.seed(1234)

fsem1 <- sem(mod, data = data, se = "robust", ordered= c("dependent"))
summary(fsem1, standardized = TRUE)
summary(fsem1, fit.measures=TRUE)
parameterestimates(fsem1)

It gives me the following error: "In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, :
lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified."

Indeed, it provides an estimate just if I remove some controls in one of the two equations.

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: matrix could not be inverted, model not identified
parts:
Hi.

There are many possible causes for this warning, including small sample.
But, I’d guess it is because you correlated the residuals of dependent and mediator despite mediator being a predictor of dependent.
dependent~ b * mediator+ cp * independent+covariates # corr errors mediator~~ dependent
